The Coin of Whimsy’s mercurial nature is felt even more so than usual in everyone’s day-to-day livelihood during the Month of Fortune. Gamblers are aflock, thieves run rampant, a rich merchant goes bankrupt, and a humble shoe cleaner stumbles upon a sack of gold on his doorstep.

It is as good a day as any to test one’s luck, and Phainon is no exception to thinking the same.

Only a day after their one-week punishment, Phainon and Mydei once again find themselves in the Marmoreal Market, flipping coins and betting on heads or tails. Established equals they may be, luck is not something that favors balance.

The coin lands on heads. The crowd claps amicably, trading bets amongst themselves for the next round, eager and excited.

Only one person does not share the sentiment.

“I can’t believe this,” Mydei groans, eyeing the coin with pure loathing like it had just managed to offend his entire ancestry.

Phainon counts a hundred drachmae’s worth of balance coins with a victorious grin on his face before shoving it into his money pouch that weighs significantly heavier than when he arrived at the market. He throws a wink at Mydei’s direction who reciprocates with a scowl of his own.

“Thank you for your generosity, kind prince,” Phainon simpers. “In honor of your ten-in-a-row loss for betting on tails, I shall let you bet on heads in the next round.”

Mydei scoffs. Thankfully, he doesn’t destroy a table this time. “Enough of this. You’ve wrung me dry, Deliverer.”

“Giving up already?” Phainon teases, unable to help himself. “A bit unusual of you, I must say.”

Their seven days of punishment together had somehow made them even closer. Only slightly, of course, considering Mydei’s aversion to friendliness and his nature of being notoriously downright hard to get along with. Nevertheless, it’s still a progress that Phainon thinks is worthy of recognition for it’s no easy feat to gain a Kremnoan’s trust.

“This is not surrender,” Mydei reiterates with his arms crossed and nose up high, exuding what Phainon would call the ‘air of a royal who finds himself above luck-based circumstances just because he’s lost consecutively.’ “I simply know where my limits lie.”

Phainon laughs at the lame excuse but doesn’t argue. It was not his intent to impoverish the crown prince of Kremnos. But seeing Mydei’s scrunched face, handsome despite the grimace, Phainon realizes that the joy in flipping coins did not stem from his victories alone.

“Alright,” he tells Mydei. “We can stop here.”

While the crowd bids their goodbye to them, Phainon takes the chance whilst Mydei is distracted to swap their money pouches in a manner that could rival the “Spirithief” Bartholos’ finesse.

Most of the balance coins in Phainon’s money pouch belonged to Mydei anyway. Phainon is simply returning what belongs to it’s original owner.

Zagreus might frown upon him for doing such a noble act, specifically during the Month of Fortune even. But Phainon values Mydei’s friendship more than the highly sought-after, fleeting favor of a Titan.

As they walk around the stalls, blatantly ignoring any calls for more entertainment, Phainon realizes that neither he nor Mydei had eaten any meals for the day, too caught up in their game of coin toss to even bother with sustenance.

Seeing as they’re about to pass by the Marmoreal Diner, Phainon turns to Mydei and asks, “Should we grab something to eat—?”

“My lords!”

Both Phainon and Mydei stop in their tracks. To their side, a man in purple carrying a stone tablet bigger than his torso rushes over to them.

“Good day,” Phainon says in greeting, a smile on his lips like a habit.

“Did you need something?” Mydei asks, tone clipped. What a charmer.

The man in purple beams upon being acknowledged by the two Chrysos Heirs. “Pardon me for interrupting your stroll, my lords. My name is Dolius.” He manages a light bow, a hand on his chest to convey sincerity. “I can’t help but notice that my lords seem to take quite the penchant for betting games.”

Mydei huffs, clearly offended. “Do not perceive me as such. I hardly know you.”

Sensing a volcano on the verge of eruption, Phainon makes a move to step in before poor Dolius is subjected to the explosive wrath of a roaring lion.

“We don’t usually engage in such activities,” Phainon explains lightly. “It’s simply because it’s the last day of the Month of Fortune that we thought it appropriate to partake in various entertainments.”

“I see.” Dolius nods slowly, seemingly pondering something before he brightens up again. “If my lords can spare the time, there’s a feast being held by the followers of Zagreus to celebrate the one extra day of the month!”

Phainon had been so caught up with his punishment that he didn’t realize Zagreus had bestowed upon them a Scarlet Month for this year.

“A feast hosted by tricksters?” Mydei clicks his tongue. “Consider me uninterested.”

Phainon sighs. “Mydei, that’s mean.”

“It is simply the truth,” Mydei shoots back.

Before Phainon could retort about how some opinions must not be said if they convey nothing but negativity, Dolius raises the stone tablet higher in favor of regaining their attention.

“The Feast of the Scarlet Month commences on the first quint of the Curtain-Fall Hour,” Dolius tells them, uncaring of the tension in between the two Chrysos Heirs in front of him. Phainon commends the dedication to promote his cause. “Look here, this is the address.”

Phainon and Mydei peer closely at the stone tablet, guided by the tip of Dolius’ finger. The address is engraved in fine inscription beneath the huge and bold letters that read,

EVERYONE IS INVITED! DRINK AND GAMBLE TO YOUR HEART’S CONTENT!

ALL HAIL ZAGREUS!

Mydei scrunches his nose in distaste. “I don’t drink. And why does it start so late?”

Phainon eyes the address. “I’m familiar with the area…”

“Deliverer, you can’t possibly be considering the idea of going.”

“Why not? It’s a leap day,” Phainon reasons. “We should savor this one extra day Zagreus gave us. Who knows, come next year, this month might end up a day short.” He turns to Dolius. “We’ll be there.”

Mydei is unable to contain his shock. “We?”

Phainon raises an eyebrow. “Not up for a challenge?”

“We do have drinking games prepared, my lords,” Dolius pipes in.

“And there you go,” Phainon says, nodding favorably at Dolius’ direction. “I’m also not an avid drinker myself, you know. Not to mention, I do believe that you haven’t had a taste of Okhema-brewn liquor just yet.”

Mydei frowns. “The only reason as to why that is so is because I have no interest in sampling alcohol.”

Phainon rethinks his tactics. “Then, consider attending for the sake of making friends.”

His tactics fail, as it always does considering that Mydei is simply an impenetrable wall of rigid principles.

“They are followers of Zagreus,” Mydei points out, affronted. “The foundations of forming amicable relationships are built from trust. Deliverer, you can’t possibly think I can make friends with the likes of them.”

At least he tried.

Phainon turns his attention back at Dolius who, thankfully, doesn’t seem at all offended by Mydei’s words. In fact, he looked quite intrigued by the exchange.

“Well,” Phainon starts. “Regardless of your opinion, I’m still going.”

Dolius smiles brightly, all crooked teeth and crinkled eye corners.

“You’ll regret it,” Mydei says.

“Won’t know until I get there,” Phainon shoots back with a shrug.

Mydei leaves him to fend for himself after that, angrily muttering something about Phainon ‘spending time with his new untrustworthy friends.’ Phainon leaves him be, no use chasing after an aggravated Mydei (he did this once and decided that not doing so yielded better results).

The theory is proven right once again when the Curtain-Fall Hour arrives and a knock lands on Phainon’s door just as he was about to leave for the Feast of the Scarlet Month.

When he flings the door open, a disgruntled Mydei greets his sights.

Phainon smiles. “Change of heart?”

“By the end of this nonsense, you’ll realize that I’m right,” Mydei replies vindictively.

When they both arrive at the address of the feast—a tavern located near the outskirts of the city—all the attendees cheer with joy at the appearance of two Chrysos Heirs.

“The heroes have come!”

“Lord Mydei, is it true that you drink blood?”

“By Kephale’s mercy, it’s indeed Lord Phainon!”

While Mydei stews in his discomfort at being hounded by a crowd of admirers, it is Phainon who does the difficult role of entertaining the lot of them with rehearsed pleasantries and smiles that do not quite reach his eyes.

“My lords!” a familiar voice calls out. Dolius emerges from the crowd after a moment’s struggle. “It’s truly a joy for my lords to have honored this humble one’s invitation. Praise be to Zagreus for this luck!”

Mydei rolls his eyes. “I’d rather eat my own fist than praise the embodiment of Trickery.”

“I apologize on his behalf,” Phainon says after a light elbow on Mydei’s ribs. “So, drinks?”

At the question, Phainon and Mydei are immediately led to a vast table filled with rows and rows of cups containing clear, amber liquid. The stench of alcohol fills the air and it admittedly makes Phainon feel a bit nauseous despite having yet to partake in a drink.

“This is the main event of the feast,” Dolius explains. “The one who finishes the most drinks gets to win ten thousand balance coins!”

The crowd goes wild at the proclamation, eagerly conversing amongst themselves and making bets on who is to take home the grand prize by the end of the feast.

Phainon turns to Mydei. “Hear that, Mydei? You can win back what you’ve lost earlier today.”

Mydei scoffs. “You assume that I am not aware of you swapping our money pouches, Deliverer. Did you really think I wouldn’t discover your schemes?”

Phainon opts to keep his mouth shut. Dolius is more than happy to occupy the silence.

“The drinks served here are the finest liquor natively brewed in Okhema,” Dolius continues. “It has also been infused with Phagousa’s blessings. With Zagreus bestowing luck upon the Scarlet Month, the odds of winning are at an all time high.”

Mydei raises an eyebrow. “From what I remember, drinking in excess is not something the Chalice of Plenty holds favor to. You speak of Their blessings when it is evident that your words are nothing but falsehoods. Dishonorable man, your lies have no effect against me.”

Phainon already feels a headache coming. He attempts to divert the topic to something else. “Dolius, has anyone accepted this… drinking game you speak of?”

“Not yet, my lord. Everyone was hoping that you would do the honors.”

The crowds await Phainon’s move with eager anticipation. Even Mydei’s golden gaze now flickered with interest despite his initial reservations.

Phainon sighs. He takes one cup, schooling his expression as he brings the rim to his lips before downing the entire drink in one go. The crowd cheers his name, a bard bursts into song, and Phainon already feels the kick of the alcohol just moments after the liquid has completely gone down his throat.

A cough makes its way past his lips, the burn of the liquor is something that Phainon is not used to. Thankfully, everyone seems to be caught up in their merriment to even notice.

All except one.

Mydei shakes his head. “This is ridiculous.”

“You forfeit?” Phainon asks, voice rough around the edges. It is a struggle to speak.

“I haven’t even agreed to going against you,” Mydei says.

Phainon takes another cup. “Shame.”

When he coughs after a rather painful and searing gulp, Mydei finally makes his amusement known, the corner of his lip curled upward in a barely there smirk.

“You know not of the ways on how to drink, Deliverer.”

Phainon attempts a laugh and regrets it immediately. His throat stings and he feels himself slowly going dizzy despite only having consumed two servings.

“I remember saying that I am not an avid drinker,” he tells Mydei. “Your Highness, if you’re amenable to do a demonstration, this amateur would be very grateful.”

Mydei’s eyebrows twitch, a telltale sign that he’s about to bite into the bait Phainon has cast. He walks towards the table, eyeing the cups with growing trepidation. Before he could grab one, however, he was stopped by Dolius’ hand on his arm.

“I forgot to tell my lords the rules of the game,” he says sheepishly before retreating his hand away after being subjected by Mydei’s sharp glower.

Mydei turns to Phainon. “You share your forgetfulness with this man, Deliverer. Or is it simply because you prefer announcing the rules after the game has commenced?”

“I prefer no such thing,” Phainon dismisses. “Dolius, if you please.”

Dolius nods. “Once you drink, you are to continue without pause. Spilling is prohibited. So, too, is making a mess. That includes regurgitation among others.”

“Reasonable,” Phainon says, feeling himself grow faint. The announcement of the rules just made the situation all the more real. “Mydei?”

Mydei responds by taking a cup and downing his drink in one sweeping motion. To his credit, he doesn’t cough like Phainon did, able to maintain his composure with ease.

Only, under close scrutiny, Phainon can see the furrow in Mydei’s eyebrows and the grimace on his lips. Mydei looks like he’s about to flip the entire table upside down and set fire to the tavern.

Seeing that Mydei has finally joined the game, the crowd erupts into applause.

“Who do you think will win?”

“Lord Mydei, for sure! I heard Kremnoans drink the blood of their victims. Fine liquor such as this is nothing to him!”

“I place my bets on Lord Phainon. He looks capable of holding his liquor.”

Phainon drowns out the noise in favor of observing Mydei as the latter picks up another cup from the table.

“I take it this is you accepting the challenge?” Phainon asks, a teasing smile on his lips. He can’t believe he actually managed to get Mydei to drink.

Mydei brings the rim of the cup close to his lips, shooting Phainon a questioning look. “Do my actions convey anything else?”

“You’re on, then.”

“Sure, Deliverer.”

A quint or more passes. Phainon has admittedly lost count of all the cups he’s managed to drink, and along with that, was his sense of reason and time.

All he remembers are sharp eyes of gold, a heavy head on his shoulder, and the familiar scent of pomegranates and something inherently sweet interlaced with a bit of spice.

Strands of blonde hair tickle the side of Phainon’s face as he struggles to maintain his balance —on his hunches with both of his hands gripping the edge of the table. Beside him, Mydei is in no better shape either, leaning against Phainon on the floor, blinking slowly and staring at nothing in particular with a face almost as red as the fabric of his garments and the marks that streaked across his exposed skin.

The world is spinning, there’s an acrid taste in his mouth, and Phainon thinks he’s on the verge of passing out. The noise in the tavern only worsens Phainon’s dizzying condition. What he would give for some peace and quiet.

“Deliverer,” comes a murmur beside him.

The sound of Mydei’s voice sobers Phainon up for just a little bit. “Are you okay?”

A sigh, softer than expected. “I’m thirsty.”

Phainon laughs. He should’ve known that Mydei wouldn’t back down so easily. It’s a shame that Phainon has to admit defeat this time.

Nevertheless, it’s comforting to know that neither of them managed to hold their liquor very well—like they had just formed some sort of an unspoken consensus that alcohol is not something to be trifled with so casually.

“Drink one more cup and it’ll be your victory,” Phainon tells Mydei, words slurring as he struggles to maintain consciousness.

Mydei shakes his head, more strands of blonde hair caress Phainon’s cheek at the action. Phainon finds that he doesn’t mind this at all.

“Not liquor,” Mydei says, barely intelligible as buries his face onto Phainon’s shoulder. “I want water.”

When he feels Mydei’s weight against him grow heavier, Phainon deduces that it’s time to take their leave. With great difficulty, he manages to scour the crowd for any signs of Dolius while supporting a half-conscious Mydei.

It probably took almost half a quint for Phainon and Mydei to bid goodbye to the followers of Zagreus with as much dignity as two men drunk out of their minds could possibly muster.

Phainon can’t even remember the reason why he participated in a drinking game and roping Mydei along with his whims. A cup is more than enough for Phainon to lose his senses, participating in drinking games should have been out of the question for someone like him.

The streets of Okhema are thankfully deserted. Perhaps it had been a good idea after all to host such a feast in the late hours or else everyone would be able to witness two drunk Chrysos Heirs navigate their way with dragging footsteps, nonsensically mumbling words into the air.

“I told you it’s ridiculous to have come,” Mydei chastises. How he’s able to maintain the signature agitation in his tone, Phainon has no idea. “Now look at us, no better than the drunken bards who make a fool of themselves.”

“I’m afraid I’m having trouble trying to spot a mirror in the area to examine our current countenance and confirm your outrageous claims,” Phainon tells him sincerely.

Mydei grunts. “We should procure one.”

“Have you got any money on you?”

“No. My money pouch was stolen by those followers of Zagreus while we were in the middle of our drinking game.”

They both stop in their tracks. Phainon’s grip on Mydei’s arm slung around his neck loosens out of shock, but not enough to release lest the poor prince loses his balance. Not like he had any in the first place for Phainon’s been supporting most of his weight this whole time.

Phainon tries to meet Mydei’s gaze, leaning down. “Mydei, you got robbed?”

Mydei nods slowly, head hanging low. “Yes.”

“And you didn’t say a thing?”

“I met eyes with the thief while he was in the process of the heist.”

Phainon could not believe his ears. “And you did nothing? You, of all people, let the thief slip away free?”

“Of course I didn’t,” Mydei retorts with an aggrieved scowl. “I told him that his face will be forever engraved in my memory until the end of times, and I will hunt him down when I’m in my peak condition.”

That sounds reassuring. It would've been far more convincing if Mydei didn't speak as if he's simply commenting on the weather instead of swearing vengeance.

“What did he look like?”

“I can’t remember,” Mydei answers casually. “I’m drunk.”

Phainon didn’t know whether to laugh or cry. There had to be at least a worth of ten thousand balance coins in Mydei’s (formerly Phainon’s) money pouch. And now it’s gone.

Sober Mydei would scour Okhema upside down until he finds the offender. Drunk Mydei, on the other hand, simply lays limp against Phainon’s side, talking as if being robbed of what most would consider a small fortune is nothing out of the ordinary.

“How much did you drink?”

Mydei is quiet for a moment. “I lost count.”

All the alcohol in Phainon’s system seemed to evaporate after this turn of events, rendering him sober.

He then ceases all talks of money just in case Mydei blinks away the haze of alcohol and remembers how he was wronged by a follower of Zagreus. Not exactly unexpected, but it was Phainon’s idea to attend the feast so by extension, the blame is his to share.

By Janus’ guidance, they were able to arrive at the entrance to the Marmoreal Palace, which was the only way they could reach the quarters dedicated to the Chrysos Heirs.

Upon seeing the pools of glistening water, Mydei peels himself away from Phainon’s hold before making his way towards the floating platform that led to the Heroes’ Baths. Phainon follows suit, confused out of his own mind.

Before Phainon could ask what Mydei was planning, the latter had already dunked his whole head into one of the pools swirling with golden waters.

Bewildered at the action, Phainon approaches, feeling silly at the sight. He debates whether or not he should take a picture, but then he realizes that Mydei hasn’t risen for air once and almost has a full-blown panic attack.

Phainon pulls Mydei back by the nape, almost collapsing in relief when he sees Mydei’s eyes blink languidly at him. He looks fine for the most part. Dazed, but fine.

“What were you thinking?” Phainon admonishes, feeling like a mother who had just discovered her son eating dirt. “Were you trying to drown yourself dead?”

“I can’t die,” was Mydei’s response.

Phainon scoffs. “Way too confident for someone who’s too drunk to function.”

“I’m thirsty.”

“And you thought that it's a brilliant idea to drink from the bath?” Phainon says, trying his hardest to keep a straight face.

Mydei says nothing. Phainon does not push the matter further, hoisting Mydei upright before laying him down on the floor, far away from any bodies of water that Mydei could use to endanger his life.

“Would you like some moment of reprieve before I carry you to your chambers?” Phainon asks, wiping Mydei’s drenched face with his sleeve, brushing away any strands of hair that stuck to the skin.

He can already hear Mydei's aggrieved response of, How dare you suggest such a crass way of transporting me!

“I’m perfectly fine where I am,” Mydei replies, eyes closed.

Phainon stares. “On the floor?”

“Yes.” Mydei confirms this with three firm nods.

“Mydei, you can’t sleep in this place.”

“I’m not. Join me down here.”

“I beg your pardon?”

Mydei huffs, exasperated, opening his eyes to throw Phainon a look that said ‘enough with the questions,’ before closing them once again. “Do as I say for once.”

Despite his befuddlement, Phainon lays down beside Mydei with his back on the floor, gazing up at the refined craftsmanship of the Marmoreal Palace’s grand ceiling.

“This is the first time I’ve felt like this,” Mydei tells him, unprompted.

Phainon tries not to place too much attention on the softness of Mydei’s voice. It is uncharacteristic, for Mydei always spoke so unambiguously in Phainon's presence—leaving no room for neither gentleness nor hesitation.

“You mean, you’ve never been drunk before?”

Mydei nods beside him. “This state of mind leaves me vulnerable.”

Phainon would like to agree wholeheartedly given that Mydei is ten thousand balance coins poorer and the thief remains to be unapprehended.

“Did you not have a good time?”

“The battlefield is the only place that caters to my enjoyment.”

Spoken like a true Kremnoan. Phainon can’t help but laugh. “You didn’t have fun even for just a little bit?”

Mydei ponders the question this time, long enough for Phainon to assume that the other has fallen asleep. Thankfully, it was not the case.

“Seeing you struggle downing a drink has contributed greatly to my amusement,” Mydei shares, a hint of a smile on his lips. “Perhaps I did enjoy myself after all.”

“At the expense of my misery, looks like.”

“Well, it was your idea to participate in a drinking game.” Mydei sighs. “I never had time for merriments such as these before I met you, Deliverer. I’m beginning to think that you’re fulfilling the role of a bad influence.”

Phainon turns to the side, disgruntled at the accusation. “You think being happy is a bad thing?”

“Such follies and nonsense divert me from my goals.”

“Has no one ever told you that being so adamant to remain miserable is never of benefit to one’s state of mind?”

Mydei was quiet. “A will lost to time had once wished for my happiness.”

Perhaps it was the inebriation. This time, Phainon lets curiosity take the reins. “Of whose?”

“My mother’s,” Mydei answers.

Phainon blinks, the statement catching him off-guard. Cautiously, he says, “She seems like a caring woman.”

“Perhaps,” Mydei says. “Even so, her tender disposition never made her any less of a warrior.”

“I never would’ve assumed as such, seeing as how her son managed to become a formidable man.”

A sober Mydei would call him out for such a blatant compliment, regarding it as an unrefined method of gaining his favor. A drunk Mydei, on the other hand, chooses to remain in contemplative silence, as if Phainon’s words hadn’t registered at all.

“My memories of my mother are little to none, and the rare dreams I have of her serve as our only connection,” Mydei says after a while. “I’ve only heard tales of her from my teacher, and he made it seem as if I was there myself witnessing all those great deeds of hers.”

“You sound like you miss her.”

Mydei huffs. “One cannot simply miss what was never there in the first place. The image of her in my mind was not one born out of knowing her myself, but of other people’s opinions of her. She sounds more like an idolized figure than a mother to me.”

“But your estrangement didn’t stop you from wanting to know more about her,” Phainon says. “You shouldn’t discount her affectionate will wishing you happiness just because you barely knew her.”

Mydei goes quiet. Phainon thinks that perhaps he might’ve pushed it too far, an apology ready at the tip of his tongue—

“Happiness hardly comes easy for someone like me,” Mydei tells him. It makes Phainon feel worse than before. “But hearing you convey your opinions regarding this matter, the fog that clouded my mind has somewhat dissipated.”

Phainon’s emotions are currently moving in between two ends of a spectrum. Just moments before, he’d been on the verge of an admonishing self-reflection, and yet now, simple words from Mydei has him almost melting into a puddle out of sheer relief.

“I’m happy to have helped with that,” Phainon says lamely.

Mydei hums, painfully unaware of Phainon’s inner turmoil. “If my mother was still alive, I have no doubts that she would have favored you immensely.”

It is known all across Amphoreus that Mydei can strike down any foe with his might. Right now, he strikes Phainon down with his words.

All coherent thoughts in Phainon’s mind vanishes pitifully without a trace upon hearing the statement uttered. To say such a thing should not be allowed.

Phainon feels his heart thud erratically within his chest. The words of a drunk man should never be of consequence. But if it’s Mydei, Phainon can’t help but make an exception out of selfish indulgence.

If Phainon’s sense of hearing were to be taken tomorrow, he would have nary a regret for Mydei’s words are enough to keep him company in a lifetime of silence.

“I’m honored that you think of me so highly, Mydei,” Phainon says, unable to stop himself from touching the end of the golden cuff that kept Mydei’s braid in place. The sight of it never fails to draw Phainon’s attention. “How could I ever manage to convey my sincerest gratitude?”

Mydei huffs, seemingly amused at the question. It’s fortunate that his eyes remain closed or else Phainon would have trouble schooling his expression to appear more dignified despite his crumbling demeanor.

“You never fail to ask the stupidest of questions, Phainon.”

Phainon has forgotten to breathe. Perhaps his sobriety had been an illusion all this time because there is no way that this conversation is real.

“You said my name,” he tells Mydei.

“It seems I have.”

“It sounds nice. I like your voice.”

“Thank you, Deliverer.”

Phainon laughs. “You are going to hate me when you wake up tomorrow.”

Mydei doesn’t respond after that, and Phainon is left to ponder the intricacies of their exchange in silence, until his own consciousness fades away.

The loud chatter that echoes incessantly is what wakes Phainon up from his dreamless sleep. When he opens his eyes, he almost passes out from shock when he realizes that his head is right at the edge of the platform that housed the Heroes’ Baths.

The sight of the Nerid Spring below is already aflock with activity—musicians livening the atmosphere, citizens engaged in productive discourse, and some leisurely others simply basking in the pleasure of being submerged in the waters blessed by Phagousa.

Phainon finds it all nauseating due to the height from where he is situated. But before he could move away from his perilous position, he finds his back colliding with something heavy and solid.

Mydei is passed out cold behind him, handsome face squished on the floor. Far from being princely-like, in Phainon’s modest opinion. He takes out his teleslate and snaps a picture.

The sound is loud enough to cause Mydei to stir in his sleep, aggravated by the loud click of his picture being taken without his knowledge. He blinks slowly, eyes of gold landing on Phainon.

“Good morning,” Phainon greets with a wince when he feels his head throb.

Mydei doesn’t respond right away. Perhaps he’s trying to get around the concept of what morning is and what’s so good about it. Or maybe he’s wondering how he’d ended up sleeping on the floor of the Heroes’ Baths.

“What time is it?” he asks Phainon after the prolonged pause.

“It’s the third quint of the Action Hour,” a smooth voice answers behind them.

Both Phainon and Mydei jolt, scampering to sit up and make themselves presentable. Phainon feels as if his head is about to split open while Mydei kept muttering curses in Kremnoan while he tries to smoothen his hair out.

Looking up, Aglaea’s imposing frame lords over them. The sight gives Phainon a strong sense of déjà vu mixed with a subtle fear that stems purely from his survival instincts.

Aglaea regards the two Chrysos Heirs with a blank expression. She looked as if she had something to say but decided against it at the last minute.

“Heroes, I apologize for cutting your merriment short for I have received some dire news,” Aglaea tells them.

Phainon struggles to follow what she’s saying while Mydei has simply given up. The latter is not even trying to conceal that his mind is elsewhere, blankly staring at a plant some ways away like he’s marvelling at the manner the verdant leaves drooped, or the sturdiness of it's stem.

Aglaea continues without mercy, “Some disciples of Janus wishes to perform a ritual welcoming the Month of Gate at the ruins of the Abyss of Fate. I’m asking you to conduct a rescue operation. Please, bring them back safely to Okhema.”

Both Phainon and Mydei nod like it’s a habit—an accustomed response for every single one of Aglaea’s orders.

“It seems that you have understood clearly,” Aglaea says.

Phainon would beg to differ, but he doubts he has enough eloquence to debate his stance against Aglaea while sporting a dreadful hangover.

“Three dromases will be prepared for you by Lady Tribbie. She will accompany you to the Abyss and help you with this mission,” Aglaea concludes when it was clear that there were no objections. “I wish you the best of luck, heroes.”

She leaves both Phainon and Mydei on the floor. Phainon rubs his aching temple with his fingers, finding the action to be futile.

“What did she say again?” he asks Mydei beside him, who currently has his head buried in his hands.

Mydei’s response comes out muffled. “...something about disciples.”

Phainon frowns, inherently dizzy. “Disciples? That’s…”

Light and hurried footsteps approach and neither Phainon nor Mydei are ready for a sudden attack. Phainon barely registers the sight of Trianne when she exclaims at a very loud voice—

“De! Snowy! Agy said you should eat something before you leave!”

The pained groans of two Chrysos Heirs could be heard. Two men thrice the size of a small child, rendered unquestionably defeated by such cheerful delivery of words. It should be considered as the humiliation of the era.

Trianne eyes them with confusion. “What’s wrong? De, Snowy, are you okay?”

Mydei is bent over the marble floor in complete agony, clutching his head out of desperation as he mutters, “Is this it? Has the Hand of Shadow come to fetch me at long last?”

Phainon, on the other hand, crawls over the edge of the platform. “Pardon me, Lady Trianne. I think I’m going to be sick—”

· · ─ ·𖥸· ─ · ·

My beloved child,

The song of slaughter might sing in your veins as it had in generations past, but let this not hinder you as you carve a new path for yourself.

As I await for your arrival in this world, I so earnestly wish for you to be merry in your youth. Make good memories and bask in the pleasure of remembrance. Form bonds, find your equal as I have done, make allies and protect each other in the face of death.

When the time comes for your rightful ascension to the throne, I hope you’ll keep these ramblings of your dear mother in mind.

— words found in a worn stone tablet that’s been discarded in the deserted halls of Kremnos’
